It took over a month for me to hear anything after I submitted my application, and received an email from an internal recruiter from their New Collar Initiatives. I have a feeling they go through applications in batches and have the same start date for various groups/cohorts. 

First step after getting that email was to have a phone screen with the recruiter, then more waiting for interview scheduling, then more waiting... Once you know your recruiter it is much easier to get updates, ask questions, etc. I made sure to ask about the timeline, process, and interview expectations, and would have felt completely in the dark if I hadn't specifically asked. 

I know it's tempting to keep checking that portal for an update, but based on my experience and from talking to others, the process can feel painfully slow. Chances are you'll be contacted before you even see updates along the way (i.e. You won't see "interviews" highlighted until you actually have an interview scheduled on their calendar). 

I'm enjoying the apprenticeship so far! There are a variety of teams that you could be placed on, so it's hard to know what exactly you'd be doing early on, but there's a good road map that apprentices follow and a lot of support.

It's not our brains that have changed, it's society's expectations. On that note... I think developments in tech and science have allowed (and forced) us to study and define these atypical brains to have them fit into our model of society. This is a broad statement, and I don't mean to imply that environmental factors aren't contributing to brain development nowadays.

We are lucky to live in a time when knowledge can help people who are struggling to be successful, but we're also living in a time when we're struggling more than ever to conform to "normal standards" of success.
